newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council working on Libya censure statement.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council working on Libya censure statement.

text.p: Security Council members began work on Monday on a statement censuring Libya for recently violating U.N. sanctions by flying an official Libyan delegation to Ghana and back, council sources said.

Libya has been the target since 1992 of mandatory U.N. sanctions, including a ban on overseas flights, for failing to extradite two men wanted by Britain and the United States for the 1988 mid-air bombing of Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, which killed 270 people.

Libya sent a letter to the Security Council last week saying that since it had allowed an American-piloted balloon to overfly its territory a few days earlier, it no longer considered itself subject to the air ban.
It later said one of its aircraft had flown an official delegation to Ghana and then returned to Tripoli. This was confirmed by a Ghanaian government minister.
U.N. council sources said permitting a balloon or any other craft to overfly Libyan territory had no bearing on the sanctions, which remained in force.
The air embargo requires other countries to deny permission to any aircraft to take off from, land in or overfly their territory if it has taken off from, or is to due to land in, Libya.

Council President Hisashi Owada of Japan told reporters after closed-door consultations there was "general agreement" the Libyan action was a violation of sanctions but the matter was "still a subject of further discussion as to exactly what ... kind of action is needed."

Council sources said members were working on a statement censuring Libya's action though it was uncertain whether it would be issued by the council president as a statement to reporters or in a more formal format.
The matter was also expected to be considered at a later date by the council's Libya sanctions committee.
